title: Post Hoc Agentic Refinement for Improving Precision in Multilingual Clinical Text De-identification

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.3 and Sec. 4 state medium verbosity and medium reasoning effort for the GPT-5 refiner; the same settings are assumed for the initial annotation pass, which the paper does not parameterise separately. max_tokens must hold one entity list per note.

task.subset_rule: WikiPII-EN, all documents, one call per entity class per document (the prompt annotates a single named entity type at a time)
task.approximation: BLOCKING - the corpus, the entity list and the per-entity guidelines are all unavailable; see open_points.

items.source: WikiPII-EN, described as "Info-boxes with people and animal descriptions derived from English Wikipedia articles (Wang et al., 2018)" with 24,145 total PII spans. The reference list resolves Wang et al. 2018 to "Describing a knowledge base" (INLG 2018), which is not a PII corpus; the better-known WikiPII (Hathurusinghe et al., PrivateNLP 2021) is a different, automatically labelled Wikipedia-biography NER set. The paper gives no download link, repository or licence for any of its three datasets.
items.config_or_split: WikiPII-EN (the only one of the three datasets that is not a clinical PHI corpus; CARMEN-ES and Transcripts-DE are hospital records)
items.fields_note: 24,145 is the number of gold PII spans, not the number of documents or of calls; the number of notes and the number of entity classes - and therefore the true call count - are not stated.

prompt.system:
You will be provided a note containing named entities.
Please identify all instances of the named entity: {ENTITY}.
Specific annotation instructions for the entity: {ENTITY_INSTRUCTION}
Respond with the entity type and the text of the entity, with one entity per line.
Here is an example for {LANGUAGE}: {EXAMPLE}
Respond with the text from the note EXACTLY.
...
If no annotations are found, respond with NO ENTITIES.
The user will provide the note to annotate.

placeholders.ENTITY: the entity class being annotated (the class list is not printed)
placeholders.EXAMPLE: the class- and language-specific few-shot example (not printed)

prompt.few_shot: few-shot, k unknown: the prompt carries one example per entity class and language, none of which is printed
prompt.verbatim: partial. The fixed scaffolding is printed in full, but the printed block contains a literal '...' before the last two lines, and the four slots {ENTITY}, {ENTITY_INSTRUCTION}, {LANGUAGE} and {EXAMPLE} are never filled in the paper: the entity class list, the per-class guidelines and the examples are all absent.

output.postprocess: one entity per line as 'type<sep>text'; the literal reply NO ENTITIES means an empty set; spans are then located back in the note
output.parse_paper: lines of entity type + surface text, matched back onto character offsets in the note

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: binary PHI/PII detection F1 at token level: an annotation counts as correct if its span overlaps a gold span regardless of entity class; precision is the share of predicted PHI/PII tokens that are correct and recall the share of gold PHI/PII tokens recovered (Sec. 3.2, Evaluation).
metric.original_location: Table 1, block 'Original GPT-5 Annotations', row WikiPII-EN (P 83.03 / R 96.85 / F1 89.41)

cost.est_note: One call per entity class per note over a corpus whose size is not reported; the triage row's 24,145 is the gold span count, not a call count. No estimate can be made until the corpus and class list are known.

open_points: Items unavailable and ambiguous: no link, repository or licence is given for WikiPII-EN, and the citation (Wang et al., 2018 = "Describing a knowledge base") does not match a PII corpus. Which corpus is meant must be settled from the public record before anything else.

The prompt cannot be filled: the entity class list, the per-class annotation guidelines and the few-shot examples are all unpublished, and the printed prompt itself elides a section with '...'. Writing them would be our own instrument.
Metric gap: token-level overlap P/R/F1 against gold character spans is not in the runner and needs a scoring hook plus a tokenisation decision.
The other two datasets are out of reach in any case: CARMEN-ES and Transcripts-DE are clinical records that need a data-use agreement.
notes: The headline contribution is the agentic refiner (Table 1, third block); the cell here is its pre-refinement baseline, which is the cleanest number attributable to gpt-5-2025-08-07 alone. || Precision 83.03 with recall 96.85 is the over-tagging pattern the paper's refiner is built to correct. || The refinement prompt (Appendix A.2) has the same unfilled {ENTITY GUIDELINES} and {EXAMPLES} slots.
runner_gaps: prompt: entity list, guidelines and few-shot examples not published
items: corpus not identified or linked
metric: token-level span-overlap F1 not implemented
